source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including all written/read and other notes, not normalized reconstructions.
source.public_versification_note: Public Judges 6–12 and Hebrew source references align one to one. All 230 original source records are bound exactly once.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retain the recurring evaluation, divine handover and seven-year period.
verses.before: The children of Israel did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD gave them into the hand of Midian seven years.
verses.after: The Israelites did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes, and he gave them into Midian’s hand for seven years.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD gave them into the hand of Midian seven years.

verses.rationale: Keep domination and forced refuge, with the rare mountain shelters rendered cautiously.
verses.before: The hand of Midian was strong against Israel. Because of Midian, the children of Israel made for themselves hiding places in the mountains, caves, and strongholds.
verses.after: Midian’s hand bore down on Israel. To escape the Midianites, the Israelites made hiding places in the mountains, caves, and strongholds.
verses.tsw_comparator: The hand of Midian was strong against Israel. Because of Midian, the children of Israel made for themselves hiding places in the mountains, caves, and strongholds.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated seasonal invasion and all three groups.
verses.before: Whenever Israel sowed, Midian, Amalek, and the people of the east came up against them.
verses.after: Whenever Israel sowed its crops, Midian, Amalek, and the eastern peoples would come up against them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whenever Israel sowed, Midian, Amalek, and the people of the east came up against them.

verses.rationale: Keep the geographical extent and explicit destruction of food and livestock.
verses.before: They camped against them and destroyed the produce of the land as far as Gaza. They left no sustenance in Israel, neither sheep nor ox nor donkey.
verses.after: They camped against them and ruined the land’s produce as far as Gaza. They left Israel nothing to live on—not a sheep, an ox, or a donkey.
verses.tsw_comparator: They camped against them and destroyed the produce of the land as far as Gaza. They left no sustenance in Israel, neither sheep nor ox nor donkey.

verses.rationale: Retain locust comparison, innumerable camels and destructive purpose; follow the reading tradition’s came.
verses.before: For they came up with their livestock and tents like locusts in abundance. They and their camels were without number, and they entered the land to destroy it.
verses.after: They came up with their livestock and tents, swarming like locusts. They and their camels were beyond counting, and they entered the land to destroy it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they came up with their livestock and tents like locusts in abundance. They and their camels were without number, and they entered the land to destroy it.

verses.rationale: Link impoverishment to the cry without turning the distress into an abstraction.
verses.before: Israel became very impoverished because of Midian, and the children of Israel cried out to the LORD.
verses.after: Midian reduced Israel to deep poverty, and the Israelites cried out to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Israel became very impoverished because of Midian, and the children of Israel cried out to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keep the repeated cry as the opening of the prophetic response across the verse boundary.
verses.before: When the children of Israel cried out to the LORD because of Midian,
verses.after: When the Israelites cried out to the LORD because of Midian,
verses.tsw_comparator: When the children of Israel cried out to the LORD because of Midian,

verses.rationale: Retain the messenger, divine speech and twofold bringing out with the slavery image.
verses.before: The LORD sent a prophet to the children of Israel, who said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I brought you up from Egypt and brought you out from the house of slavery.
verses.after: he sent them a prophet, who said, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I brought you up from Egypt. I brought you out of the house of slavery.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD sent a prophet to the children of Israel, who said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I brought you up from Egypt and brought you out from the house of slavery.

verses.rationale: Preserve both hands, rescue, expulsion and the land gift.
verses.before: I delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of everyone who oppressed you. I drove them out before you and gave you their land.
verses.after: I rescued you from Egypt’s hand and from the hand of everyone who oppressed you. I drove them out before you and gave you their land.
verses.tsw_comparator: I delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all who oppressed you. I drove them out before you and gave you their land.

verses.rationale: Keep fear as allegiance and the accusation in nested divine speech.
verses.before: I said to you, ‘I am the LORD your God. You will not fear the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live.’ But you have not listened to my voice.”
verses.after: I told you, “I am the LORD your God. You must not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you live.” But you have not obeyed my voice.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And I said to you, ‘I am the LORD your God. You shall not fear the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live.’ But you have not listened to my voice.”

verses.rationale: Clarify father and son while preserving the unusual place of threshing and its stated purpose.
verses.before: The messenger of the LORD came and sat under the oak at Ophrah, which belonged to Joash the Abiezrite. Gideon his son was beating out wheat in the winepress to hide it from Midian.
verses.after: The angel of the LORD came and sat beneath the terebinth at Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite. Joash’s son Gideon was beating out wheat in the winepress to keep it from Midian.
verses.tsw_comparator: The messenger of the LORD came and sat under the oak at Ophrah, which belonged to Joash the Abiezrite. Gideon his son was beating out wheat in the winepress to hide it from Midian.

verses.rationale: Preserve the greeting’s force beside Gideon’s hiding without explaining it as irony or prediction.
verses.before: The messenger of the LORD appeared to him and said, “The LORD is with you, mighty warrior.”
verses.after: The angel of the LORD appeared to him and said, “The LORD is with you, mighty warrior.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The messenger of the LORD appeared to him and said, “The LORD is with you, mighty warrior.”

verses.rationale: Keep Gideon’s protest, collective us and accusation as his speech, not narrator commentary.
verses.before: Gideon said to him, “Please, my lord, if the LORD is with us, why then has all this happened to us? Where are all his wonders that our ancestors told us about, saying, ‘Did not the LORD bring us up from Egypt?’ But now the LORD has abandoned us and given us into the hand of Midian.”
verses.after: “Please, my lord,” Gideon replied, “if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us? Where are all his wonders our ancestors told us about when they said, ‘Did not the LORD bring us up from Egypt?’ Now the LORD has abandoned us and given us into Midian’s grasp.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Gideon said to him, “Please, my lord, if the LORD is with us, why then has all this happened to us? Where are all his wonders that our ancestors told us about, saying, ‘Did not the LORD bring us up from Egypt?’ But now the LORD has abandoned us and given us into the hand of Midian.”

verses.rationale: Keep the shift from angel to LORD and the unexplained reference to Gideon’s strength.
verses.before: The LORD turned to him and said, “Go in this strength of yours, and you will save Israel from the hand of Midian. Have I not sent you?”
verses.after: The LORD turned to him and said, “Go with this strength of yours and rescue Israel from Midian’s grasp. Am I not sending you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD turned to him and said, “Go in this strength of yours, and you shall save Israel from the hand of Midian. Have I not sent you?”

verses.rationale: Preserve clan and household distinctions and the claim of low standing; note youngest/least.
verses.before: He said to him, “Please, Lord, how can I save Israel? Look, my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house.”
verses.after: “Please, Lord,” he answered, “how can I rescue Israel? My clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the youngest in my father’s household.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to him, “Please, Lord, how can I save Israel? Look, my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house.”

verses.rationale: Retain divine presence and the one-man image.
verses.before: The LORD said to him, “But I will be with you, and you will strike Midian as one man.”
verses.after: The LORD told him, “I will be with you, and you will strike Midian down as if it were one man.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to him, “But I will be with you, and you shall strike Midian as one man.”

verses.rationale: Keep the favor idiom and uncertainty over the speaker’s identity.
verses.before: Gideon said to him, “If now I have found favor in your eyes, then give me a sign that it is you who speak with me.
verses.after: Gideon said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, give me a sign that it is you speaking with me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gideon said to him, “If now I have found favor in your eyes, then give me a sign that it is you who speak with me.

verses.rationale: Keep the request and answer, allowing Gideon’s speech to continue from the prior verse.
verses.before: Please do not depart from here until I come to you, bring out my gift, and set it before you.” And he said, “I will stay until you return.”
verses.after: Please do not leave until I return with my offering and set it before you.” He answered, “I will stay until you return.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Please do not depart from here until I come to you, bring out my gift, and set it before you.” And he said, “I will stay until you return.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the substantial ancient measure, food, containers and tree setting.
verses.before: Gideon went in and prepared a young goat and unleavened cakes from an ephah of flour. He put the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot, brought them out to him under the oak, and presented them.
verses.after: Gideon went in and prepared a young goat and unleavened bread from an ephah of flour. He put the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot, brought them out beneath the terebinth, and presented them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gideon went in and prepared a young goat and unleavened cakes from an ephah of flour. He put the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot, brought them out to him under the oak, and presented them.

verses.rationale: Retain angel of God rather than harmonizing the title, and all three food instructions.
verses.before: The messenger of God said to him, “Take the meat and the unleavened cakes, lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth.” And he did so.
verses.after: The angel of God told him, “Take the meat and unleavened bread, place them on that rock, and pour out the broth.” Gideon did so.
verses.tsw_comparator: The messenger of God said to him, “Take the meat and the unleavened cakes, lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth.” And he did so.

verses.rationale: Preserve the staff, fire’s origin and disappearance without adding an ascent.
verses.before: Then the messenger of the LORD reached out the tip of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened cakes. Fire rose from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened cakes, and the messenger of the LORD disappeared from his sight.
verses.after: The angel of the LORD reached out the tip of the staff in his hand and touched the meat and unleavened bread. Fire rose from the rock and consumed them, and the angel of the LORD vanished from Gideon’s sight.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the messenger of the LORD reached out the tip of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened cakes. Fire rose from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened cakes, and the messenger of the LORD disappeared from his sight.

verses.rationale: Keep recognition, alarm and face-to-face language.
verses.before: Gideon saw that he was the messenger of the LORD, and Gideon said, “Alas, Lord GOD! For now I have seen the messenger of the LORD face to face.”
verses.after: Gideon realized that it was the angel of the LORD. “Ah, Lord GOD!” he said. “I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Gideon saw that he was the messenger of the LORD, and Gideon said, “Alas, Lord GOD! For now I have seen the messenger of the LORD face to face.”

verses.rationale: Retain peace before the assurances, linking it to the altar’s name.
verses.before: But the LORD said to him, “Peace to you. Do not fear; you will not die.”
verses.after: The LORD told him, “Peace to you. Do not be afraid; you will not die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD said to him, “Peace to you. Do not fear; you shall not die.”

verses.rationale: Keep the spoken assurance as the altar name and exact location.
verses.before: Then Gideon built an altar there to the LORD and called it “The LORD Is Peace.” To this day it stands at Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
verses.after: Gideon built an altar to the LORD there and named it “The LORD Is Peace.” It is still at Ophrah of the Abiezrites to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Gideon built an altar there to the LORD and called it “The LORD Is Peace.” To this day it stands at Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

verses.rationale: Preserve the difficult two-bull wording rather than silently collapsing it to one animal.
verses.before: That night the LORD said to him, “Take your father’s bull, the second bull seven years old, and tear down the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the Asherah beside it.
verses.after: That night the LORD told him, “Take your father’s bull and the second bull, seven years old. Tear down your father’s altar to Baal and cut down the Asherah beside it.
verses.tsw_comparator: That night the LORD said to him, “Take your father’s bull, the second bull seven years old, and tear down the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the Asherah beside it.

verses.rationale: Keep altar arrangement, second bull and cult object used as fuel; note uncertainty of arrangement term.
verses.before: Build an altar to the LORD your God on top of this stronghold in proper order. Take the second bull and offer it as a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah that you cut down.”
verses.after: Build a properly arranged altar to the LORD your God on top of this stronghold. Take the second bull and offer it as a burnt offering, using the wood of the Asherah you cut down.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Build an altar to the LORD your God on top of this stronghold in proper order. Take the second bull and offer it as a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah that you cut down.”

verses.rationale: Preserve ten, fear and nighttime action without replacing fear with moral judgment.
verses.before: So Gideon took ten men from among his servants and did as the LORD had spoken to him. But because he feared his father’s household and the people of the city too much to do it by day, he did it by night.
verses.after: Gideon took ten of his servants and did what the LORD had told him. He was afraid of his father’s household and the men of the town, so he did it at night instead of by day.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Gideon took ten men from among his servants and did as the LORD had spoken to him. But because he feared his father’s household and the people of the city too much to do it by day, he did it by night.

verses.rationale: Keep the three discoveries and repeated second bull.
verses.before: When the people of the city rose early in the morning, look, the altar of Baal was torn down, the Asherah beside it was cut down, and the second bull had been offered on the altar that had been built.
verses.after: When the men of the town got up early, they found Baal’s altar demolished, the Asherah beside it cut down, and the second bull offered on the newly built altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the people of the city rose early in the morning, look, the altar of Baal was torn down, the Asherah beside it was cut down, and the second bull had been offered on the altar that had been built.

verses.rationale: Retain inquiry leading to identification rather than inventing witnesses.
verses.before: They said to one another, “Who did this thing?” When they searched and inquired, they said, “Gideon son of Joash did this thing.”
verses.after: “Who did this?” they asked one another. They investigated and searched until they said, “Gideon son of Joash did it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to one another, “Who did this thing?” When they searched and inquired, they said, “Gideon son of Joash did this thing.”

verses.rationale: Keep the explicit demand for death and both stated charges.
verses.before: Then the people of the city said to Joash, “Bring out your son so that he may die, because he tore down the altar of Baal and cut down the Asherah beside it.”
verses.after: The men of the town told Joash, “Bring your son out. He must die, because he demolished Baal’s altar and cut down the Asherah beside it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the people of the city said to Joash, “Bring out your son so that he may die, because he tore down the altar of Baal and cut down the Asherah beside it.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the legal wordplay, threat and challenge without softening the father’s speech.
verses.before: Yet Joash said to everyone who stood against him, “Will you contend for Baal? Will you save him? Whoever contends for him will be put to death by morning. If he is a god, let him contend for himself, because someone tore down his altar.”
verses.after: Joash answered everyone confronting him, “Are you going to plead Baal’s case? Are you going to save him? Anyone who pleads for him must be put to death by morning! If he is a god, let him plead his own case, since someone has torn down his altar.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Joash said to all who stood against him, “Will you contend for Baal? Will you save him? Whoever contends for him shall be put to death by morning. If he is a god, let him contend for himself, because someone tore down his altar.”

verses.rationale: Explain the name through the narrator’s own wordplay while leaving naming agent implicit.
verses.before: So on that day Gideon was called Jerubbaal, saying, “Let Baal contend against him,” because he tore down his altar.
verses.after: That day Gideon was named Jerubbaal, meaning, “Let Baal contend with him,” because he had torn down Baal’s altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore on that day Gideon was called Jerubbaal, saying, “Let Baal contend against him,” because he tore down his altar.

verses.rationale: Preserve three groups, crossing and named valley without supplying the river.
verses.before: Now all Midian, Amalek, and the people of the east gathered together, crossed over, and camped in the Valley of Jezreel.
verses.after: All Midian, Amalek, and the eastern peoples gathered together, crossed over, and camped in the Jezreel Valley.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now all Midian, Amalek, and the people of the east gathered together, crossed over, and camped in the Valley of Jezreel.

verses.rationale: Retain the Spirit clothing himself with Gideon as a garment, not reversing the image.
verses.before: But the Spirit of the LORD clothed Gideon, and he blew the ram’s horn. The Abiezrites were called out to follow him.
verses.after: The Spirit of the LORD clothed himself with Gideon. Gideon sounded the horn, and the Abiezrites rallied behind him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the Spirit of the LORD clothed Gideon, and he blew the ram’s horn. The Abiezrites were called out to follow him.

verses.rationale: Keep the sequence and all four tribal names, with plural meeting party retained.
verses.before: He sent messengers throughout all Manasseh, and they also were called out to follow him. He sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they went up to meet them.
verses.after: He sent messengers throughout Manasseh, and they too rallied behind him. He also sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they came up to meet them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent messengers throughout all Manasseh, and they also were called out to follow him. He sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they went up to meet them.

verses.rationale: Keep the conditional appeal open across the verse boundary.
verses.before: Gideon said to God, “If you will save Israel by my hand, as you have spoken,
verses.after: Gideon said to God, “If you are going to rescue Israel through my hand as you have said,
verses.tsw_comparator: Gideon said to God, “If you will save Israel by my hand, as you have spoken,

verses.rationale: Preserve the precise first test and repeated promised rescue.
verses.before: look, I am laying a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If dew is on the fleece alone and all the ground is dry, then I will know that you will save Israel by my hand, as you have spoken.”
verses.after: look, I am laying a wool fleece on the threshing floor. If dew falls only on the fleece while all the ground is dry, I will know that you will rescue Israel through my hand, as you have said.”
verses.tsw_comparator: look, I am laying a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If dew is on the fleece alone and all the ground is dry, then I will know that you will save Israel by my hand, as you have spoken.”

verses.rationale: Keep timing, both squeezing verbs and the full bowl.
verses.before: And so it happened. He rose early the next morning, squeezed the fleece, and wrung enough dew from the fleece to fill a bowl with water.
verses.after: That is what happened. Gideon got up early the next day, squeezed the fleece, and wrung out a bowlful of water.
verses.tsw_comparator: And so it happened. He rose early the next morning, squeezed the fleece, and wrung enough dew from the fleece to fill a bowl with water.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated just-once request, divine anger and reversed conditions.
verses.before: Then Gideon said to God, “Do not let your anger burn against me. Let me speak only once more. Please let me test only once more with the fleece. Let the fleece alone be dry, and let there be dew on all the ground.”
verses.after: Then Gideon said to God, “Do not let your anger burn against me. Let me speak just once more. Please let me test the fleece just this once: let the fleece alone be dry, with dew on all the ground.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Gideon said to God, “Do not let your anger burn against me. Let me speak only once more. Please let me test only once more with the fleece. Let the fleece alone be dry, and let there be dew on all the ground.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the exact reversal without turning the event into a general guidance rule.
verses.before: God did so that night. The fleece alone was dry, and there was dew on all the ground.
verses.after: God did that very night as Gideon asked. Only the fleece was dry; dew covered all the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God did so that night. The fleece alone was dry, and there was dew on all the ground.

verses.rationale: Keep both names and relative geography.
verses.before: Jerubbaal—that is, Gideon—and all the people who were with him rose early and camped beside the spring of Harod. The camp of Midian was north of them, by the hill of Moreh in the valley.
verses.after: Jerubbaal—that is, Gideon—and all the people with him rose early and camped by the spring of Harod. Midian’s camp lay north of them, in the valley by the hill of Moreh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jerubbaal—that is, Gideon—and all the people who were with him rose early and camped beside the spring of Harod. The camp of Midian was north of them, by the hill of Moreh in the valley.

verses.rationale: Retain the hand-to-hand contrast and the stated risk of boasting.
verses.before: The LORD said to Gideon, “The people who are with you are too many for me to give Midian into their hand, lest Israel boast against me, saying, ‘My own hand saved me.’
verses.after: The LORD told Gideon, “You have too many people for me to give Midian into their hand. Israel might boast against me and say, ‘My own hand saved me.’
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Gideon, “The people who are with you are too many for me to give Midian into their hand, lest Israel boast against me, saying, ‘My own hand saved me.’

verses.rationale: Preserve Gilead despite geographical difficulty, unusual departure verb and both numbers.
verses.before: So now proclaim in the hearing of the people, saying, ‘Whoever is afraid and trembling, let him turn back and depart from Mount Gilead.’” Twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, and ten thousand remained.
verses.after: Now announce for everyone to hear: ‘Anyone who is afraid and trembling may turn back and leave Mount Gilead.’” Twenty-two thousand turned back, and ten thousand remained.
verses.tsw_comparator: So now proclaim in the hearing of the people, saying, ‘Whoever is afraid and trembling, let him turn back and depart from Mount Gilead.’” Twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, and ten thousand remained.

verses.rationale: Keep the refining/sifting test and repeated divine selection without a character test added.
verses.before: The LORD said to Gideon, “The people are still too many. Bring them down to the water, and I will test them for you there. Whoever I say to you, ‘This one will go with you,’ will go with you; and whoever I say, ‘This one will not go with you,’ will not go.”
verses.after: The LORD told Gideon, “There are still too many. Bring them down to the water, and I will sift them for you there. Whoever I tell you is to go with you will go. Whoever I tell you is not to go will not go.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Gideon, “The people are still too many. Bring them down to the water, and I will test them for you there. Whoever I say to you, ‘This one shall go with you,’ shall go with you; and whoever I say, ‘This one shall not go with you,’ shall not go.”

verses.rationale: Retain the two drinking groups as described, without inventing tactical vigilance.
verses.before: So he brought the people down to the water. The LORD said to Gideon, “Everyone who laps the water with his tongue as a dog laps, set by himself; likewise everyone who kneels down to drink.”
verses.after: Gideon brought the people down to the water. The LORD said, “Set apart everyone who laps the water with his tongue as a dog laps, and everyone who kneels down to drink.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So he brought the people down to the water. The LORD said to Gideon, “Everyone who laps the water with his tongue as a dog laps, set by himself; likewise everyone who kneels down to drink.”

verses.rationale: Keep hand-to-mouth action alongside preceding dog image and exact count.
verses.before: The number of people who lapped, putting their hands to their mouths, was three hundred men. All the rest of the people knelt down to drink water.
verses.after: Three hundred men lapped with their hands to their mouths. All the rest knelt down to drink water.
verses.tsw_comparator: The number of those who lapped, putting their hands to their mouths, was three hundred men. All the rest of the people knelt down to drink water.

verses.rationale: Retain the selected group, divine rescue and dismissal.
verses.before: The LORD said to Gideon, “With the three hundred men who lapped I will save you and give Midian into your hand. Let all the other people go, each to his place.”
verses.after: The LORD told Gideon, “With the three hundred men who lapped, I will rescue you and give Midian into your hand. Let everyone else go home.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Gideon, “With the three hundred men who lapped I will save you and give Midian into your hand. Let all the other people go, each to his place.”

verses.rationale: Keep transfer of supplies and horns, identifying the retained group without concealing compressed syntax.
verses.before: So the three hundred took the provisions of the people in their hands and their ram’s horns. Gideon sent all the men of Israel away, each to his tent, but kept the three hundred men. The camp of Midian was below him in the valley.
verses.after: The men took the people’s provisions and horns. Gideon sent the rest of Israel back to their tents but kept the three hundred. Midian’s camp was below him in the valley.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the three hundred took the provisions of the people in their hands and their ram’s horns. Gideon sent all the men of Israel away, each to his tent, but kept the three hundred men. The camp of Midian was below him in the valley.

verses.rationale: Preserve nighttime command and divine gift expressed as accomplished.
verses.before: That night the LORD said to him, “Rise, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand.
verses.after: That night the LORD told him, “Get up and go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: That night the LORD said to him, “Rise, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand.

verses.rationale: Keep the offered accommodation to fear and the named servant.
verses.before: But if you are afraid to go down, go down to the camp with Purah your servant,
verses.after: But if you are afraid to go down, take your servant Purah with you to the camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you are afraid to go down, go down to the camp with Purah your servant,

verses.after: When the Israelites saw that Abimelech was dead, each went home.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, they departed, each to his place.

verses.rationale: Retain narrator’s divine repayment judgment and unchanged stated count.
verses.before: Thus God returned the evil of Abimelech that he had done to his father by killing his seventy brothers.
verses.after: So God returned upon Abimelech the evil he had done to his father by killing his seventy brothers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus God returned the evil of Abimelech that he had done to his father by killing his seventy brothers.

verses.rationale: Preserve heads image and explicit link to Jotham’s curse.
verses.before: God returned all the evil of the men of Shechem upon their heads, and the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.
verses.after: God also brought all the evil of Shechem’s men back on their own heads. The curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God returned all the evil of the men of Shechem upon their heads, and the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.

verses.rationale: Keep three generations, tribal identity and location without inventing a battle.
verses.before: After Abimelech, Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, arose to save Israel. He lived at Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
verses.after: After Abimelech, Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, an Issacharite, arose to rescue Israel. He lived at Shamir in Ephraim’s hill country.
verses.tsw_comparator: After Abimelech, Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, arose to save Israel. He lived at Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.

verses.rationale: Retain judge title, exact period and burial notice.
verses.before: He judged Israel twenty-three years. Then he died and was buried at Shamir.
verses.after: He judged Israel for twenty-three years. Then he died and was buried at Shamir.
verses.tsw_comparator: He judged Israel twenty-three years. Then he died and was buried at Shamir.

verses.rationale: Keep succession, regional identity and distinct duration.
verses.before: After him Jair the Gileadite arose and judged Israel twenty-two years.
verses.after: After him arose Jair the Gileadite, who judged Israel for twenty-two years.
verses.tsw_comparator: After him Jair the Gileadite arose and judged Israel twenty-two years.

verses.rationale: Preserve three thirties, animals and towns, with the Hebrew soundplay noted.
verses.before: He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty towns, called Havvoth-Jair to this day, which are in the land of Gilead.
verses.after: He had thirty sons who rode thirty donkeys. They had thirty towns in Gilead, called Havvoth-jair to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty towns, called Havvoth-Jair to this day, which are in the land of Gilead.

verses.rationale: Keep the short independent burial notice.
verses.before: Jair died and was buried at Kamon.
verses.after: Jair died and was buried at Kamon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jair died and was buried at Kamon.

verses.rationale: Retain all seven worship groups and repeated service contrasted with abandonment.
verses.before: The children of Israel again did evil in the eyes of the LORD and served the Baals, the Ashtaroth, the gods of Aram, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines. They abandoned the LORD and did not serve him.
verses.after: Again the Israelites did what was evil in the LORD’s eyes. They served the Baals and the Ashtaroth, the gods of Aram, Sidon, Moab, the Ammonites, and the Philistines. They abandoned the LORD and did not serve him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel again did evil in the eyes of the LORD and served the Baals, the Ashtaroth, the gods of Aram, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines. They abandoned the LORD and did not serve him.

verses.rationale: Keep divine selling and both oppressors.
verses.before: The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the children of Ammon.
verses.after: The LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines and the Ammonites.
verses.tsw_comparator: The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the children of Ammon.

verses.rationale: Retain both temporal notices and the specific eastern group rather than silently reconciling chronology.
verses.before: They crushed and oppressed the children of Israel that year. For eighteen years they oppressed all the children of Israel who were beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.
verses.after: That year they shattered and crushed the Israelites. For eighteen years they oppressed all the Israelites east of the Jordan, in the Amorite land of Gilead.
verses.tsw_comparator: They crushed and oppressed the children of Israel that year. For eighteen years they oppressed all the children of Israel who were beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.

verses.rationale: Keep widening invasion and all three groups.
verses.before: The children of Ammon crossed the Jordan to fight also against Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim, so Israel was greatly distressed.
verses.after: The Ammonites crossed the Jordan to fight Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim’s household as well. Israel was in deep distress.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Ammon crossed the Jordan to fight also against Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim, so Israel was greatly distressed.

verses.rationale: Retain confession’s specific acts and change from you to our God.
verses.before: The children of Israel cried out to the LORD, saying, “We have sinned against you, for we have abandoned our God and served the Baals.”
verses.after: The Israelites cried out to the LORD, “We have sinned against you. We abandoned our God and served the Baals.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel cried out to the LORD, saying, “We have sinned against you, for we have abandoned our God and served the Baals.”

verses.rationale: Supply the implied rescue verb while preserving all four initial names and question.
verses.before: The LORD said to the children of Israel, “Did I not save you from Egypt, from the Amorites, from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines?
verses.after: The LORD answered the Israelites, “Did I not rescue you from Egypt, the Amorites, the Ammonites, and the Philistines?
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to the children of Israel, “Did I not save you from Egypt, from the Amorites, from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines?

verses.rationale: Preserve Maon rather than harmonizing the textual variant Midian and keep three further peoples.
verses.before: And when the Sidonians, Amalekites, and Maonites oppressed you and you cried out to me, I saved you from their hand.
verses.after: The Sidonians, Amalek, and Maon oppressed you too. You cried out to me, and I rescued you from their hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the Sidonians, Amalekites, and Maonites oppressed you and you cried out to me, I saved you from their hand.

verses.rationale: Keep the force of refusal before the later compassionate response.
verses.before: Yet you have abandoned me and served other gods. Therefore I will save you no more.
verses.after: Yet you abandoned me and served other gods. So I will not rescue you again.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet you have abandoned me and served other gods. Therefore I will save you no more.

verses.rationale: Retain the sharp challenge and repeated rescue word.
verses.before: Go and cry out to the gods whom you have chosen. Let them save you in the time of your distress.”
verses.after: Go and cry out to the gods you chose! Let them rescue you in your time of distress.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Go and cry out to the gods whom you have chosen. Let them save you in the time of your distress.”

verses.rationale: Preserve submission, eyes idiom and urgent plea.
verses.before: The children of Israel said to the LORD, “We have sinned. Do to us whatever is good in your eyes; only please deliver us this day.”
verses.after: The Israelites said to the LORD, “We have sinned. Do to us whatever seems good in your eyes. Only rescue us today, please.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel said to the LORD, “We have sinned. Do to us whatever is good in your eyes; only please deliver us this day.”

verses.rationale: Keep actual removal and service, rendering the shortened-soul idiom without claiming forgiveness is stated.
verses.before: So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD, and his soul became impatient over the misery of Israel.
verses.after: They removed the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD. He could no longer bear Israel’s misery.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD, and his soul became impatient over the misery of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep the two assemblies and different camps.
verses.before: Then the children of Ammon were gathered together and camped in Gilead. The children of Israel gathered together and camped at Mizpah.
verses.after: The Ammonites were called to arms and camped in Gilead. The Israelites gathered and camped at Mizpah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the children of Ammon were gathered together and camped in Gilead. The children of Israel gathered together and camped at Mizpah.

verses.rationale: Retain people/leaders phrasing and promised headship that leads into Jephthah’s negotiation.
verses.before: The people, the leaders of Gilead, said to one another, “Who is the man who will begin to fight against the children of Ammon? He will become head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”
verses.after: The people, the leaders of Gilead, asked one another, “Who will begin the fight against the Ammonites? He will be head over everyone living in Gilead.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The people, the leaders of Gilead, said to one another, “Who is the man who will begin to fight against the children of Ammon? He shall become head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”

verses.rationale: Preserve martial strength and both parents without shifting stigma into narrator abuse.
verses.before: Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty warrior, but he was the son of a prostitute. Gilead was Jephthah’s father.
verses.after: Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty warrior. His mother was a prostitute, and Gilead was his father.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty warrior, but he was the son of a prostitute. Gilead was Jephthah’s father.

verses.rationale: Keep exclusion, inheritance and the brothers’ stated reason as their speech.
verses.before: Gilead’s wife also bore him sons. When the wife’s sons grew up, they drove Jephthah out and said to him, “You will not inherit in our father’s house, for you are the son of another woman.”
verses.after: Gilead’s wife also bore him sons. When they grew up, they drove Jephthah out. “You will have no inheritance in our father’s household,” they said, “because you are another woman’s son.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Gilead’s wife also bore him sons. When the wife’s sons grew up, they drove Jephthah out and said to him, “You shall not inherit in our father’s house, for you are the son of another woman.”

verses.rationale: Retain narrator’s description without adding details of unreported raids.
verses.before: So Jephthah fled from his brothers and lived in the land of Tob. Worthless men gathered around Jephthah and went out with him.
verses.after: Jephthah fled from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob. Worthless men gathered around him and went out with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Jephthah fled from his brothers and lived in the land of Tob. Worthless men gathered around Jephthah and went out with him.

verses.rationale: Keep broad timing and outbreak of war.
verses.before: After some time, the children of Ammon fought against Israel.
verses.after: Some time later the Ammonites went to war with Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: After some time, the children of Ammon fought against Israel.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated war setting and elders initiating recall.
verses.before: When the children of Ammon fought against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah from the land of Tob.
verses.after: When the Ammonites fought Israel, Gilead’s elders went to bring Jephthah back from the land of Tob.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the children of Ammon fought against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah from the land of Tob.

verses.rationale: Keep commander distinct from head of the whole community.
verses.before: They said to Jephthah, “Come and be our commander, so that we may fight against the children of Ammon.”
verses.after: “Come and be our commander,” they told him, “so we can fight the Ammonites.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to Jephthah, “Come and be our commander, so that we may fight against the children of Ammon.”

verses.rationale: Retain his charge against the elders without correcting it to brothers alone.
verses.before: Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, “Did you not hate me and drive me out from my father’s house? Why have you come to me now when you are in distress?”
verses.after: Jephthah answered the elders, “Did you not hate me and drive me out of my father’s household? Why come to me now that you are in trouble?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, “Did you not hate me and drive me out from my father’s house? Why have you come to me now when you are in distress?”

verses.rationale: Keep the response’s ambiguous therefore and expanded offer of headship.
verses.before: The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “For this reason we have now returned to you: that you may go with us, fight against the children of Ammon, and become head over us, over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”
verses.after: Gilead’s elders replied, “That is why we have come back to you now. Come with us, fight the Ammonites, and be our head—over everyone living in Gilead.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “For this reason we have now returned to you: that you may go with us, fight against the children of Ammon, and become head over us, over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the conditional negotiation and divine victory condition.
verses.before: Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, “If you bring me back to fight against the children of Ammon, and the LORD gives them before me, will I become your head?”
verses.after: Jephthah told them, “If you bring me back to fight the Ammonites and the LORD gives them over to me, I will be your head.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, “If you bring me back to fight against the children of Ammon, and the LORD gives them before me, shall I become your head?”

verses.rationale: Retain the hearing-witness image and solemn pledge.
verses.before: The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “The LORD will be witness between us if we do not do according to your word.”
verses.after: The elders answered, “May the LORD listen between us: we will do as you say.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “The LORD will be witness between us if we do not do according to your word.”

verses.rationale: Keep both offices, people’s appointment and public sacred setting.
verses.before: So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and commander over them. Jephthah spoke all his words before the LORD at Mizpah.
verses.after: Jephthah went with Gilead’s elders, and the people made him their head and commander. At Mizpah he spoke all his terms before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and commander over them. Jephthah spoke all his words before the LORD at Mizpah.

verses.rationale: Preserve personal territorial claim and the relational challenge.
verses.before: Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon, saying, “What is between me and you, that you have come to me to fight against my land?”
verses.after: Jephthah sent messengers to the Ammonite king: “What is there between you and me, that you have come to fight in my land?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon, saying, “What is between me and you, that you have come to me to fight against my land?”

verses.rationale: Retain contested claim and all three river limits as royal speech.
verses.before: The king of the children of Ammon said to Jephthah’s messengers, “Because Israel took away my land when they came up from Egypt, from the Arnon as far as the Jabbok and to the Jordan. Now therefore restore it peacefully.”
verses.after: The Ammonite king told Jephthah’s messengers, “When Israel came up from Egypt, they took my land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and the Jordan. Now give it back peacefully.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of the children of Ammon said to Jephthah’s messengers, “Because Israel took away my land when they came up from Egypt, from the Arnon as far as the Jabbok and to the Jordan. Now therefore restore it peacefully.”

verses.rationale: Keep renewed embassy connected to the message in the next verse.
verses.before: Jephthah again sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon,
verses.after: Jephthah sent messengers back to the Ammonite king
verses.tsw_comparator: Jephthah again sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon,

verses.rationale: Keep formal introduction and explicit denial naming both peoples.
verses.before: and said to him, “Thus says Jephthah: Israel did not take away the land of Moab or the land of the children of Ammon.
verses.after: with this answer: “This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites.
verses.tsw_comparator: and said to him, “Thus says Jephthah: Israel did not take away the land of Moab or the land of the children of Ammon.

verses.rationale: Preserve the route and source sea name with established vocabulary.
verses.before: But when they came up from Egypt, Israel went through the wilderness as far as the Sea of Reeds and came to Kadesh.
verses.after: When Israel came up from Egypt, they traveled through the wilderness to the Sea of Reeds and reached Kadesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when they came up from Egypt, Israel went through the wilderness as far as the Sea of Reeds and came to Kadesh.

verses.rationale: Keep both refusals as given in Jephthah’s retelling, without harmonizing other travel accounts.
verses.before: Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Please let me pass through your land,’ but the king of Edom did not listen. They also sent to the king of Moab, but he would not consent. So Israel remained at Kadesh.
verses.after: Israel sent messengers to Edom’s king, saying, ‘Please let me pass through your land.’ But Edom’s king would not listen. They also sent to Moab’s king, who refused. So Israel stayed at Kadesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Please let me pass through your land,’ but the king of Edom did not listen. They also sent to the king of Moab, but he would not consent. So Israel remained at Kadesh.

verses.rationale: Retain route, eastward approach and repeated boundary explanation.
verses.before: Then they went through the wilderness, went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab, came from the east side of the land of Moab, and camped beyond the Arnon. They did not enter the territory of Moab, for the Arnon was the border of Moab.
verses.after: Then they traveled through the wilderness around Edom and Moab, came to Moab’s eastern side, and camped beyond the Arnon. They did not enter Moab’s territory, for the Arnon was its boundary.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they went through the wilderness, went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab, came from the east side of the land of Moab, and camped beyond the Arnon. They did not enter the territory of Moab, for the Arnon was the border of Moab.

verses.rationale: Keep king’s two designations and destination request, smoothing collective person shift.
verses.before: Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, king of Heshbon. Israel said to him, ‘Please let us pass through your land to our place.’
verses.after: Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled at Heshbon. They said, ‘Please let us pass through your land to our own place.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, king of Heshbon. Israel said to him, ‘Please let us pass through your land to our place.’

verses.rationale: Preserve mistrust, complete assembly and battle site.
verses.before: Yet Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory. Sihon gathered all his people, camped at Jahaz, and fought against Israel.
verses.after: But Sihon would not trust Israel to cross his territory. He gathered all his people, camped at Jahaz, and fought Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory. Sihon gathered all his people, camped at Jahaz, and fought against Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep divine-gift argument and conquest in the speaker’s voice.
verses.before: The LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they struck them. So Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites who inhabited that land.
verses.after: The LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his people into Israel’s hand, and Israel struck them down. Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites who lived there.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they struck them. So Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites who inhabited that land.

verses.rationale: Retain both axes and all boundaries.
verses.before: They took possession of all the territory of the Amorites, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan.
verses.after: They took all Amorite territory, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan.
verses.tsw_comparator: They took possession of all the territory of the Amorites, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan.

verses.rationale: Keep challenge and dispossession argument without endorsing it as modern land policy.
verses.before: So now the LORD, the God of Israel, has dispossessed the Amorites before his people Israel. Should you then dispossess us?
verses.after: Now that the LORD, the God of Israel, has driven the Amorites out before his people Israel, are you going to take possession of their land?
verses.tsw_comparator: So now the LORD, the God of Israel, has dispossessed the Amorites before his people Israel. Should you then dispossess us?

verses.rationale: Retain Chemosh in an address to Ammon’s king and the parallel divine-possession claims; note relationship and wording ambiguity.
verses.before: Will you not possess whatever Chemosh your god gives you to possess? And whatever the LORD our God dispossesses before us, that we will possess.
verses.after: Do you not possess what Chemosh your god gives you to possess? We too will possess the land of all those the LORD our God has driven out before us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Will you not possess whatever Chemosh your god gives you to possess? And whatever the LORD our God dispossesses before us, that we will possess.

verses.rationale: Keep both rhetorical questions and Jephthah’s version of Balak’s actions.
verses.before: Now are you really better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever contend with Israel, or did he ever fight against them?
verses.after: Are you really better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever dispute with Israel or fight them?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now are you really better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever contend with Israel, or did he ever fight against them?

verses.rationale: Preserve exact duration and both town groups without chronological recalculation.
verses.before: While Israel has lived in Heshbon and its villages, Aroer and its villages, and in all the cities along the Arnon for three hundred years, why did you not recover them during that time?
verses.after: Israel has lived in Heshbon and its dependent towns, Aroer and its dependent towns, and all the towns along the Arnon for three hundred years. Why did you not recover them during that time?
verses.tsw_comparator: While Israel has lived in Heshbon and its villages, Aroer and its villages, and in all the cities along the Arnon for three hundred years, why did you not recover them during that time?

verses.rationale: Keep reciprocal wrong and judge repetition as the closing appeal.
verses.before: I therefore have not sinned against you, but you are doing evil to me by fighting against me. May the LORD, the Judge, judge this day between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon.”
verses.after: I have not wronged you, but you are doing me wrong by fighting me. May the LORD, the Judge, judge today between the Israelites and the Ammonites.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I therefore have not sinned against you, but you are doing evil to me by fighting against me. May the LORD, the Judge, judge this day between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon.”

verses.rationale: Retain rejection of the full embassy.
verses.before: But the king of the children of Ammon did not listen to the words Jephthah sent to him.
verses.after: But the Ammonite king would not listen to the message Jephthah sent him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the king of the children of Ammon did not listen to the words Jephthah sent to him.

verses.rationale: Keep Spirit before the vow and the repeated route without making the vow divinely commanded.
verses.before: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh, passed through Mizpeh of Gilead, and from Mizpeh of Gilead he passed on to the children of Ammon.
verses.after: The Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah. He passed through Gilead and Manasseh, then through Mizpeh of Gilead. From Mizpeh of Gilead he went on toward the Ammonites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh, passed through Mizpeh of Gilead, and from Mizpeh of Gilead he passed on to the children of Ammon.

verses.rationale: Keep emphatic conditional vow and Jephthah as its initiator.
verses.before: Jephthah vowed a vow to the LORD and said, “If you truly give the children of Ammon into my hand,
verses.after: Jephthah made a vow to the LORD: “If you really give the Ammonites into my hand,
verses.tsw_comparator: Jephthah vowed a vow to the LORD and said, “If you truly give the children of Ammon into my hand,

verses.rationale: Retain personal encounter, peace, dedication and sacrifice linked by and; note whatever and alternative reading without erasing force.
verses.before: then whatever comes out from the doors of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the children of Ammon will belong to the LORD, and I will offer it up as a burnt offering.”
verses.after: whoever comes out through the doors of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the Ammonites will belong to the LORD, and I will offer that one as a burnt offering.”
verses.tsw_comparator: then whatever comes out from the doors of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the children of Ammon shall belong to the LORD, and I will offer it up as a burnt offering.”

verses.rationale: Keep gift of victory without asserting it was purchased by the vow.
verses.before: So Jephthah crossed over to the children of Ammon to fight against them, and the LORD gave them into his hand.
verses.after: Jephthah crossed over to fight the Ammonites, and the LORD gave them into his hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Jephthah crossed over to the children of Ammon to fight against them, and the LORD gave them into his hand.

verses.rationale: Preserve every place, twenty towns and extent of defeat.
verses.before: He struck them from Aroer as far as the approach to Minnith, twenty cities, and as far as Abel-Keramim, with a very great slaughter. So the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel.
verses.after: He struck them from Aroer to the approach to Minnith—twenty towns—and as far as Abel-keramim, in a crushing defeat. The Ammonites were subdued before the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: He struck them from Aroer as far as the approach to Minnith, twenty cities, and as far as Abel-Keramim, with a very great slaughter. So the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep matching came-out-to-meet language, celebration and double statement of only child.
verses.before: Jephthah came to his house at Mizpah, and look, his daughter came out to meet him with tambourines and dances. She was his only child; besides her he had neither son nor daughter.
verses.after: When Jephthah reached his home at Mizpah, his daughter came out to meet him with tambourines and dancing. She was his only child; he had no other son or daughter.

verses.rationale: Preserve his distress and blame as his speech, not a narrator judgment on the daughter.
verses.before: When he saw her, he tore his clothes and said, “Alas, my daughter! You have brought me very low, and you have become one who troubles me, for I have opened my mouth to the LORD and cannot turn back.”
verses.after: When he saw her, he tore his clothes and said, “Ah, my daughter! You have brought me very low. You have become one of those who trouble me! I have opened my mouth to the LORD and cannot take it back.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When he saw her, he tore his clothes and said, “Alas, my daughter! You have brought me very low, and you have become one who troubles me, for I have opened my mouth to the LORD and cannot turn back.”

verses.rationale: Keep her actual reply, mouth repetition and vengeance interpretation without adding consent language.
verses.before: She said to him, “My father, you have opened your mouth to the LORD. Do to me according to what has gone out from your mouth, since the LORD has given you vengeance against your enemies, the children of Ammon.”
verses.after: She answered, “My father, you have opened your mouth to the LORD. Do to me what came out of your mouth, now that the LORD has taken vengeance for you on your enemies, the Ammonites.”
verses.tsw_comparator: She said to him, “My father, you have opened your mouth to the LORD. Do to me according to what has gone out from your mouth, since the LORD has given you vengeance against your enemies, the children of Ammon.”

verses.rationale: Keep two months, female companions and virginity as the object of lament; note unusual descent wording.

verses.rationale: Retain female remembrance, unnamed daughter and four-day annual custom; note lament/commemorate range.

verses.rationale: Retain two hand images and the counterchallenge.
